4.1.title: Therapeutic indications
4.1.text:
VaxRabeo is indicated for pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis against rabies in individuals of all age groups.

VaxRabeo should be used in accordance with official recommendations.

4.2.title: Posology and method of administration
4.2.text:
Posology

One dose of the reconstituted vaccine consists of 0.5 mL (entire vial content) for intramuscular administration or 0.1 mL for intradermal administration.

Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) Primary series Individuals can be vaccinated according to one of the vaccination schedules presented in Table 1 and in accordance with official recommendations when available.

Booster dose A booster dose consists of one dose of 0.5 mL given by intramuscular route or one dose of 0.1 mL given by intradermal route in accordance with WHO recommendations. Booster doses and/or regular serology testing of rabies virus neutralising antibodies may be indicated according to official recommendations.

Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) PEP should be initiated as soon as possible after suspected exposure to rabies. In all cases, proper wound care (careful washing of all bites and scratches with soap or detergent and copious amounts of water and/or virucidal agents) must be performed immediately or as soon as possible after exposure. It must be performed before administration of rabies vaccine or rabies immunoglobulins, when they are indicated.

The rabies vaccine administration must be performed strictly in accordance with the category of exposure, the patient immune status, the animal’s status for rabies, and according to official recommendations (see Table 2 for WHO recommendations).

For category III exposure (WHO classification, see Table 2), rabies immunoglobulin should be administered concomitantly with the vaccine. In this case, each dose of the vaccine should be administered at a body site distant from the immunoglobulin administration sites, if possible.

Vaccination should not be discontinued unless the animal is declared not rabid according to a veterinarian assessment (supervision of animal and/or laboratory analysis).

PEP of individuals previously immunised According to WHO recommendations, previously immunised individuals are individuals who have documented evidence of previous PrEP or already received PEP or who discontinued PEP after receiving at least two vaccinations. These individuals should receive 1 dose of vaccine intramuscularly (0.5 mL) or intradermally (0.1 mL) on Days 0 and 3.

Rabies immunoglobulin is not indicated for previously immunised individuals.

These schedules should not apply to immunocompromised individuals.

Interchangeability No interchangeability studies have been conducted with VaxRabeo during a PrEP course or a PEP course. According to WHO recommendations:
-     Where continuation with the same rabies vaccine is not possible, another rabies vaccine may be used to complete the vaccination course.
-     If unavoidable, the route of administration may be changed during a PEP or a PrEP course.

Immunocompromised individuals PrEP Serology testing of neutralising antibodies should be performed after completion of the primary series (see Table 1), and after each booster dose to assess the possible need for an additional dose of the vaccine. Official recommendations for immunocompromised individuals should be followed.

PEP Only vaccination schedules listed in Table 3 must be administered. Serology testing of neutralising antibodies may be indicated. Official recommendations for immunocompromised individuals should be followed. Rabies immunoglobulins should be given concomitantly with the vaccine for both category II & III exposures in all cases, even if previously immunised (see Table 2 for category definition).

Paediatric population The doses and vaccination schedules for paediatric population are the same as those for adults, with the exception that the intradermal PEP IPC regimen is for paediatric individuals only.

Method of administration

VaxRabeo is for intramuscular or intradermal use only.

Intramuscular use The vaccine (0.5 mL) is administered in the anterolateral region of the thigh muscle in infants and young children and in the deltoid muscle in older children and adults.

Intradermal use The vaccine (0.1 mL) is administered in the upper arm or the forearm, or the anterolateral thigh, or suprascapular region.

When 2 doses of rabies vaccine are administered at the same visit, they should be injected in 2 different sites/limbs.

For administration precautions, see section 4.4.

For concomitant administration with other vaccines or other medicinal product including rabies immunoglobulin, see section 4.5.

For instructions on reconstitution of the medicinal product before administration, see section 6.6.

4.3.title: Contraindications
4.3.text:
PrEP

Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

PEP

Since rabies infection almost always results in death, there are no contraindications to post-exposure vaccination (see section 4.4).

4.4.title: Special warnings and precautions for use
4.4.text:
Traceability

In order to improve the traceability of biological medicinal products, the name and the batch number of the administered product should be clearly recorded.

Hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis

Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been observed with vaccines. Appropriate medical treatment and supervision should always be readily available in the event of an anaphylactic reaction following administration of VaxRabeo.

In individuals who have experienced an anaphylactic reaction following a dose of VaxRabeo, the risk of developing rabies must be carefully considered in decisions regarding the discontinuation of PEP vaccination.

Hypersensitivity to neomycin

Although antibiotics are not used in the manufacturing process, neomycin is present in the starting materials. Therefore, undetectable traces of neomycin might be present in the vaccine. Caution should be exercised when the vaccine is administered to individuals with hypersensitivity to this antibiotic.

Anxiety-related reactions

Anxiety-related reactions, including vasovagal reactions (syncope), hyperventilation or stress-related reactions, may occur in association with vaccination as a psychogenic response to the needle injection. Procedures should be in place to avoid injury from fainting and to manage syncope.

Concurrent illness

For PrEP, administration of VaxRabeo should be postponed in individuals suffering from moderate or severe acute illness with or without fever.

Thrombocytopenia and coagulation disorders

As with all injectable vaccines, VaxRabeo should be administered with caution to individuals with thrombocytopenia or a bleeding disorder since bleeding may occur following an intramuscular administration.

Immunocompromised individuals

VaxRabeo has not been studied in immunocompromised individuals.

Individuals with congenital or acquired immunodeficiency may have reduced immune response to the vaccine. Therefore, it is recommended to serologically monitor RVNA (Rabies Virus Neutralising Antibodies) level in such individuals to ensure that an acceptable immune response has been induced. Additional vaccine doses should be given as necessary per official recommendations (see sections 4.2 and 4.5).

Moreover, if post-exposure vaccination is needed, only schedules of vaccination listed in Table 3 for previously non-immunised individuals should be administered. In addition, rabies immunoglobulin should be given concomitantly with the vaccine for category II & III exposures in all cases, even if previously immunised (see section 4.2).

Limitations of vaccine effectiveness

As with any vaccine, vaccination with VaxRabeo may not protect 100% of vaccinated individuals. In order to reach a sufficient level of neutralising antibodies for protection, recommendations for the use of VaxRabeo must be strictly followed (see section 4.2) as an insufficient immune response may lead to fatal cases of rabies.

Rabies PEP should not be interrupted due to any adverse reactions; serious adverse reactions are rare and need careful management (see section 4.8).

Administration precautions

Do not inject into the gluteal area as administration in this area may result in lower neutralising antibody titres.

It is essential that intradermal administration of VaxRabeo is carried out only by medical staff trained in this technique in order to ensure that the vaccine is delivered intradermally. For the intradermal route, appropriate syringe and needle should be used.

Excipients with known effect

Phenylalanine This vaccine contains 19.8 micrograms phenylalanine per dose (0.5 mL). Phenylalanine may be harmful for people with phenylketonuria (PKU), a rare genetic disorder in which phenylalanine builds up because the body cannot remove it properly.

Proline This vaccine contains 13.8 micrograms of proline per dose (0.5 mL). In patients suffering from hyperprolinaemia, exposure to proline should be minimised. This vaccine should be used in patients suffering from hyperprolinaemia only if strictly necessary.

Sodium This vaccine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per dose (0.5 mL), that is to say essentially ‘sodium-free’.

Sorbitol This vaccine contains 6 mg sorbitol per dose (0.5 mL). The additive effect of concomitantly administered medicinal products containing sorbitol (or fructose) and dietary intake of sorbitol (or fructose) should be taken into account.

4.8.title: Undesirable effects
4.8.text:
Summary of the safety profile

In adults, the most frequently reported adverse reactions were injection site pain by intradermal use (44.2%) and by intramuscular use (40.5%), myalgia (32%), headache (21.4%) and malaise (16.5%).

In the paediatric population, the most frequently reported local adverse reactions were injection site tenderness/pain by intramuscular use (58.7%) and injection site swelling by intradermal use (47.3%).

In children 12 months to 23 months of age, the most frequently reported systemic adverse reactions were crying abnormal (47.4%) and irritability (47.4%), and in children 2 years of age and above, the most frequently reported systemic adverse reaction was myalgia (37.7%).

The following adverse reactions were more frequently reported in paediatric population than in adults: injection site tenderness/pain (intramuscular use) (58.7% and 40.5% respectively), injection site erythema (intradermal use) (35.7% and 0% respectively), injection site swelling (intradermal use) (47.3% and 0% respectively), fever (10.6% and 1.3% respectively).

The reported adverse reactions were mostly mild (Grade 1) or moderate (Grade 2) in intensity, occurred within 3 days after vaccination, and mostly resolved spontaneously after 1 to 3 days.

The reactogenicity profile was comparable after each of the consecutive priming doses.

The most frequently reported adverse reactions after a booster dose of VaxRabeo by intramuscular use were generally consistent with those reported during primary series: local pain, myalgia, malaise and headache. The frequency of these reactions was generally comparable to, or lower than, that observed after the primary series.

Tabulated list of adverse reactions

A pooled safety analysis was performed on 5 observer-blind, randomised, controlled clinical studies conducted in adults 18 years of age and older (VRV11, VRV12, VRV13, VRV00014 and VRV09) and in children 1 to 17 years of age (VRV12 and VRV09). The pooled safety analysis included 1 906 participants who received at least one dose of VaxRabeo in PrEP (primary series vaccination) or in PEP regimens, with a 6-month safety follow-up after last vaccination. Of the 1 906 participants, 1 665 participants received VaxRabeo by intramuscular route (1 360 adults and 305 children including 17 children 12 months to 23 months of age) and 241 participants received VaxRabeo by intradermal route (129 adults and 112 children including 2 children 12 months to 23 months of age). Overall, 664 adults received the first dose of VaxRabeo on Day 0 concomitantly with human rabies immunoglobulins (HRIG), in the studies evaluating PEP.

The adverse reactions listed in Table 4 were reported after any dose of VaxRabeo in adults and children from 1 year of age and older during clinical studies (pooled safety analysis of 5 clinical studies).

Adverse reactions are listed by MedDRA system organ class according to the following frequency convention: very common (≥ 1/10), common (≥ 1/100 to < 1/10), uncommon (≥ 1/1 000 to < 1/100), rare (≥ 1/10 000 to < 1/1 000), very rare (< 1/10 000). Reporting of suspected adverse reactions

Reporting suspected adverse reactions after authorisation of the medicinal product is important. It allows continued monitoring of the benefit/risk balance of the medicinal product. 5.1.title: Pharmacodynamic properties
5.1.text:
Pharmacotherapeutic group: Rabies vaccines, ATC code: J07BG01

Mechanism of action

VaxRabeo consists of purified inactivated rabies virus (WISTAR strain PM/WI38 1503-3M) produced in cell culture. Administration of VaxRabeo induces production of rabies-virus neutralising antibodies (RVNA) directed against the surface glycoprotein of the rabies virus.

Clinical immunology

In the absence of clinical efficacy data, a post-vaccination RVNA titre threshold of 0.5 IU/mL has been applied as a surrogate immune marker of protection to infer efficacy of VaxRabeo, as per WHO recommendation.

Five clinical studies have been conducted to assess the immunogenicity of VaxRabeo in PrEP and PEP, by measuring the levels of RVNA. Immunogenicity results presented for the per protocol analysis set (PPAS) are based on participants who were seronegative at baseline.

In VRV12 study, the immunogenicity persistence was assessed 12 months (M12) after 3-dose PrEP. The post-booster immune response was assessed 14 days after booster dose administration with VaxRabeo at M12.

An anamnestic response was observed in all participants after a booster dose of VaxRabeo administered regardless of the type of rabies vaccine received in primary series.

Paediatric population

An intermediate formulation of VaxRabeo (that contained half the quantity of antigen, and lacked recombinant Human Albumin (rHA)), given by intramuscular route, was assessed in two clinical studies conducted in paediatric participants: VRV06 study for PrEP and VRV08 study for PEP. Data generated with the final formulation are presented below (VRV12 and VRV09 studies).
